Issues.Title: fix(oxide): relax engines.node to >= 10 for @tailwindcss/oxide
Issues.Body:
## Summary

### What
Relaxes `engines.node` from `>= 20` to `>= 10` for `@tailwindcss/oxide` and all 12 native platform packages (`crates/node/package.json` + `crates/node/npm/*/`). Adds changelog fragment `.changelog/oxide-engines-node.md`.

### Why
`@tailwindcss/oxide` ships prebuilt N-API binaries compiled against **N-API 3**, which is stable since Node.js 10.0.0. The `>= 20` constraint was introduced in `c6f0c6b3` as part of the Node 20 build-toolchain bump; it reflects build-time requirements, not runtime compatibility. It unnecessarily blocks `npm install` on Node 14/16/18 LTS environments that fully support N-API 3, forcing upgrades for CI pipelines, Docker images, and legacy systems.

### How
- Set `"engines": { "node": ">= 10" }` in:
  - `crates/node/package.json` (main package)
  - All 12 native platform packages under `crates/node/npm/` (android-arm-eabi, android-arm64, darwin-arm64, darwin-x64, freebsd-x64, linux-arm-gnueabihf, linux-arm64-gnu, linux-arm64-musl, linux-x64-gnu, linux-x64-musl, win32-arm64-msvc, win32-x64-msvc)
- No Rust or JS source changes needed — metadata-only fix.

**Edge case — WASM excluded:** `crates/node/npm/wasm32-wasi/package.json` is intentionally left unchanged at `"node": "^20.19.0 || ^22.13.0 || >=23.5.0"`. The WASI runtime genuinely requires a modern Node; relaxing it to `>= 10` would be incorrect.

**Changelog fragment:** `.changelog/oxide-engines-node.md`
```md
### Changed

- Relax `engines.node` for `@tailwindcss/oxide` from `>= 20` to `>= 10` to reflect N-API runtime compatibility ([tailwindlabs/tailwindcss#20491](https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/issues/20491))
```

Fixes #20491

## Test plan

### Engine check
```sh
node -e "const fs=require('fs');[
'crates/node/package.json',
'crates/node/npm/android-arm-eabi/package.json',
'crates/node/npm/android-arm64/package.json',
'crates/node/npm/darwin-arm64/package.json',
'crates/node/npm/darwin-x64/package.json',
'crates/node/npm/freebsd-x64/package.json',
'crates/node/npm/linux-arm-gnueabihf/package.json',
'crates/node/npm/linux-arm64-gnu/package.json',
'crates/node/npm/linux-arm64-musl/package.json',
'crates/node/npm/linux-x64-gnu/package.json',
'crates/node/npm/linux-x64-musl/package.json',
'crates/node/npm/win32-arm64-msvc/package.json',
'crates/node/npm/win32-x64-msvc/package.json'
].forEach(f=>console.log(f+': '+JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(f,'utf8')).engines.node))"
```
Output (all `>= 10`):
```

crates/node/npm/android-arm-eabi/package.json: >= 10
crates/node/npm/android-arm64/package.json: >= 10
```

### WASM edge case check

```sh
# ^20.19.0 || ^22.13.0 || >=23.5.0  (unchanged, as intended)
```


Issues.Title: Fix unshipped relative imports in `@tailwindcss/node` type declarations
Issues.Body:
Fixes #20631

## Summary

`@tailwindcss/node`'s `dist/index.d.ts` / `dist/index.d.mts` start with seven imports of modules the package doesn't ship (`./ast`, `./candidate`, `./compile`, `./intellisense`, `./theme`, `./utilities`, `./variants`), so consumers with `skipLibCheck: false` get TS errors.

They come from `__unstable__loadDesignSystem`'s inferred return type. Inferring it makes the declaration bundler follow `tailwindcss`'s internal `DesignSystem` type (which isn't exported from `tailwindcss`) into its source files, and those files end up as relative imports in the bundle.

This annotates the return type as `ReturnType<typeof ___unstable__loadDesignSystem>`, i.e. the type of the function imported from `tailwindcss`. The declarations now only import from `'tailwindcss'`, which consumers can resolve. No runtime change and no tsup config change.

## Test plan

Added `integrations/node/types.test.ts`. It installs the packed `tailwindcss` and `@tailwindcss/node` tarballs into a project with `skipLibCheck: false` and runs `tsc` on a file that calls `compile()` and `__unstable__loadDesignSystem()`.

```sh
pnpm build
pnpm vitest --root=./integrations node/types.test.ts
```

- With this change: passes.
- With `compile.ts` reverted: fails, because of the seven unresolved imports.

The test uses `"target": "ESNext"` because the declarations also reference `Disposable` / `Symbol.dispose` (from `Instrumentation`), which need the ESNext lib. That's unrelated to this issue.

I ran this locally by building and packing only `tailwindcss` and `@tailwindcss/node`, since I don't have the Rust toolchain set up. `vitest run packages/@tailwindcss-node` also passes. I haven't run the full suite.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Fix unshipped relative imports in `@tailwindcss/node` type declarations" (#20632)

Issues.Title: Skip the `color-mix(…)` polyfill without a color interpolation method
Issues.Body:
## Summary

This is a follow-up to https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20658, which fixes a crash in the same polyfill. This PR doesn't depend on it, and can merge before or after it.

The `color-mix(…)` polyfill assumes that each `color-mix(…)` starts with `in <colorspace>,`. But in CSS Color 5 the color interpolation method is optional (it defaults to `oklab`):

```
color-mix( <color-interpolation-method>? , [ <color> && <percentage [0,100]>? ]#)
```

When a `color-mix(…)` contains `currentcolor` or a variable that isn't in the theme, the polyfill uses the node after the first `,` as the fallback. Without `in`, that node is the second color, not the first one:

| Input in `.foo { color: … }`                           | Fallback before | Fallback after |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | --------------- | -------------- |
| `color-mix(currentcolor 50%, transparent)`             | `#0000`         | none           |
| `color-mix(var(--unknown), red)`                       | `red`           | none           |
| `color-mix(in oklab, currentcolor 50%, transparent)`   | `currentColor`  | `currentColor` |

For a theme variable without `in`, e.g. `color-mix(var(--color-red-500) 50%, transparent)`, the fallback was `color-mix(oklch(…) 50%, transparent)`. Lightning CSS doesn't compute a `color-mix(…)` without a color interpolation method, so a browser without `color-mix(…)` drops that fallback anyway.

This PR skips the polyfill for a `color-mix(…)` whose first non-separator node isn't the word `in`. The check ignores leading whitespace and comments before `in`, e.g. `color-mix( in oklab, …)` or `color-mix(/* … */ in oklab, …)` in a custom property.

It also adds the optional chain on `colorspace?.kind`, so that e.g. `color-mix(in)` doesn't crash. https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20658 adds the same optional chain. When both merge, expect a small conflict on that line. The test of 20658 (`works without a color interpolation method and with a single color`) expects a fallback and an `@supports` rule. With this PR, that output changes on purpose: no fallback and no `@supports` rule.

## Test plan

- Added three tests to the `color-mix(…)` polyfill tests in `packages/tailwindcss/src/index.test.ts`:
  - `color-mix(…)` without a color interpolation method (`currentcolor`, an unknown variable, a theme variable, and a single theme variable) gets no fallback. This test fails without the change.
  - `color-mix( in oklab, currentcolor 50%, transparent)` with a leading space keeps its `currentColor` fallback. This guards the leading separator check.
  - `--tint: color-mix(/* tint */ in oklab, currentcolor 50%, transparent)` keeps its `currentcolor` fallback. Custom properties keep their comments, and the value parser has no comment node, so the check drops comments before it looks for `in`.
- `env -u NODE_ENV pnpm exec vitest run` in `packages/tailwindcss`: 5191 passed, 1 skipped.
- `pnpm run build` in `packages/tailwindcss` passes.
- `pnpm changelog check` passes, and `prettier --check` passes on the changed files.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Skip the `color-mix(…)` polyfill without a color interpolation method" (#20666)

Issues.Title: Make the integration tests resilient to slow package installs
Issues.Body:
This PR makes the integration tests more resilient to slow package installs.

Since about 18:00 UTC on 2026-11-04, the Linux runners download packages from the npm registry slowly (some tarballs at about 22 KiB/s, and some metadata requests take 13 to 17 seconds). Two runs on `main` failed because of it:

- https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/actions/runs/41887340047
- https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/actions/runs/41899669095

There were 3 problems:

1. The harness runs `pnpm install` inside the 60s timeout of the test. On a slow network, the install alone takes most of that time.
2. When a test times out, vitest only says "Test timed out". The log does not say which command hangs, and the command keeps running in the background.
3. The 3 "half-upgraded" tests in `integrations/upgrade/upgrade-errors.test.ts` had `retry: 0`. The bun test also installs its dependencies again with `bun` in the test, so one slow install failed the job.

## Changes

- The harness tracks each command of `exec` until it exits. When a test fails, it prints each command that still runs, with its duration and its output so far. Then it stops that command and the processes that it started. The cleanup is registered before the install, so it also covers an install that hangs.
- The install has a timeout of its own (120s, 240s on Windows), and the timeout of the test starts after the install. Both timeouts name the commands that still run. The timeout of vitest stays as a backstop.
- The half-upgraded tests get the CI default of 2 retries. Each attempt runs in a new temporary directory, so a retry is safe. The bun test gets a timeout of 120s.

## Test plan

- A test with a command that hangs (`echo "partial output" && sleep 37`, with a 2s timeout) now fails with the name of the command and its output, and no `sleep` process is left after the test.
- A test whose `pnpm install` takes 4s now passes with a 2s test timeout. Before this change, it failed with "Test timed out in 2000ms".
- The PostCSS and CLI config integration tests pass locally.

<sub>Sent by an AI assistant on behalf of @RobinMalfait.</sub>
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Make the integration tests resilient to slow package installs" (#20669)

Issues.Title: Prefix relative selectors with \:scope\ inside \@scope\ rules
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Fixes #20668

When a nested `@scope (&)` rule is hoisted out of a style rule (e.g. in custom `@utility` definitions like daisyUI's `join`), rules inside the scope that use relative selectors (such as `> .item`) are emitted as-is. Under a top-level `@scope`, Lightning CSS cannot parse a relative selector directly and drops the rule with an `Invalid empty selector` warning.

Per CSS Cascading and Inheritance Level 6 §3.2, relative selectors inside `@scope` match relative to the scoping root and behave identically to prefixing the selector with `:scope`.

This PR updates `handleNesting` in `packages/tailwindcss/src/ast.ts`:
- Identifies rules inside `@scope` that begin with a combinator (relative selectors, e.g. `> .item`, `+ .sibling`).
- Prepends `:scope` to each relative selector (e.g. `:scope > .item`), which is semantically identical, valid CSS, and accepted cleanly by Lightning CSS during downstream optimization.

## Test plan

- Added unit tests in `packages/tailwindcss/src/ast.test.ts` verifying that relative selectors under hoisted `@scope` receive `:scope > ...` prefixes.
- Added an integration test in `packages/tailwindcss/src/index.test.ts` compiling a utility containing `@scope (&)` with `> .item` matching the reported reproduction.
- Verified test suite passes:
```
pnpm vitest run packages/tailwindcss/src/ast.test.ts packages/tailwindcss/src/index.test.ts
```
Output:
```
 ✓  tailwindcss  src/ast.test.ts (209 tests) 138ms
 ✓  tailwindcss  src/index.test.ts (260 tests) 1005ms

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  469 passed (469)
```
- Checked formatting:
```
pnpm prettier --check packages/tailwindcss/src/ast.ts packages/tailwindcss/src/ast.test.ts packages/tailwindcss/src/index.test.ts
```
Output:
```
All matched files use Prettier code style!
```

Issues.Title: Ignore `<!--` and `-->` between top-level rules in the CSS parser
Issues.Body:
## Summary

The CSS parser treats `-->` as the start of a custom property, so `parse('-->')` throws `Invalid custom property, expected a value`. `a { color: red } --> b { color: blue }` turns rule `b` and everything after it into one fake declaration, including `@tailwind utilities`. `<!--` also sticks to the next selector, or throws before an at-rule.

CSS Syntax 3 ignores these tokens at the top level of a stylesheet, and Lightning CSS already does. This PR skips them between top-level nodes. Inside a selector, a custom property value or a block nothing changes.

## Test plan

- New tests in `css-parser.test.ts`: 8 fail without the fix, all 208 pass with it.
- `corepack pnpm@11.9.0 exec vitest run` in `packages/tailwindcss`: 5204 passed, 1 skipped.
- `pnpm changelog check` passes.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Ignore `<!--` and `-->` between top-level rules in the CSS parser" (#20665)

Issues.Title: @tailwindcss/turbopack: README's `as: '*.css'` breaks CSS modules
Issues.Body:
**What version of Tailwind CSS are you using?** v4.3.4 (`tailwindcss` and `@tailwindcss/turbopack`) **What build tool (or framework if it abstracts the build tool) are you using?** Next.js 16.4.4 (Turbopack) **What version of Node.js are you using?** v24.22.1 **What browser are you using?** N/A (fails at build time) **What operating system are you using?** macOS **Reproduction URL** https://github.com/kachkaev/tailwind-turbopack-css-module-repro **Describe your issue** The `@tailwindcss/turbopack` README configures the loader with `as: '*.css'`. Because the rule matches `*.module.css` files too, `as` turns every CSS module into plain global CSS, so any app with a CSS module breaks: - **App router only:** the build passes, but `import styles from './page.module.css'` gives `styles.box === undefined`. The page renders `

`, and `.box` is emitted as an unscoped global rule. - **With a pages-router page that imports the same module:** the build fails: ``` Failed to write app endpoint /page Caused by: - [project]/app/page.module.css [ssr] (css module) - Expected process result to be a module, but it was ignored ``` Removing `as` fixes both cases: every file keeps its own module type, the class is scoped (`O2dkuW_box`), and Tailwind utilities are still generated. ```js module.exports = { turbopack: { rules: { '*.css': { loaders: ['@tailwindcss/turbopack'], }, }, }, } ``` The integration test in `integrations/turbopack/loader.test.ts` only imports a `globals.css`, so it doesn't catch this. Dropping `as` from the README and the test, and adding a CSS module to the test, would cover it.

Issues.Title: Don't break CSS modules in the `@tailwindcss/turbopack` README setup
Issues.Body:
## Summary

The `@tailwindcss/turbopack` README sets `as: '*.css'` on the `*.css` rule. That rule also matches `*.module.css`, so `as` turns every CSS module into plain global CSS: `styles.box` is `undefined` in the app router, and a pages router page that imports the same module fails the build with "Expected process result to be a module, but it was ignored".

This PR removes `as` from the README and from the loader integration tests. Without it, each file keeps its own module type, and the loader still runs on it.

Fixes #20659

## Test plan

- New test in `integrations/turbopack/loader.test.ts` that imports a `page.module.css` with `@apply underline`. It checks that the page gets the scoped class, and that the served CSS has the scoped class and the `underline` declaration. It fails with `as: '*.css'` and passes without it.
- `pnpm build`, then `pnpm vitest --root=./integrations run turbopack/loader.test.ts`: all 3 tests pass.
- `pnpm changelog check` passes.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Don't break CSS modules in the `@tailwindcss/turbopack` README setup" (#20660)

Issues.Title: Fix `@tailwindcss/oxide-wasm32-wasi` hanging forever when it loads
Issues.Body:
## Summary

`@tailwindcss/oxide-wasm32-wasi@4.3.4` hangs forever when it loads, for example with `NAPI_RS_FORCE_WASI=error node -e "require('@tailwindcss/oxide')"` in Node 24, or in a WebContainer. Version 4.3.3 works.

The `.wasm` file of 4.3.4 does not export `_initialize`. All other exports are the same as in 4.3.3. Without `_initialize`, the thread setup of wasi-libc never runs, and Rust's std loops forever in `pthread_key_delete` when the module registers.

`napi-build` links `crt1-reactor.o` and adds `--export=_initialize` only when it finds the file at `$RUSTC/../../lib/rustlib/<target>/lib/self-contained/crt1-reactor.o`. Otherwise it prints only a warning. https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20651 moved the release job to `macos-latest` (`macos-26-arm64`). There, Cargo gives a bare `rustc` in `$RUSTC`, so the path is empty. The [v4.3.4 release log](https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/actions/runs/41526897752) shows:

```
warning: tailwind-oxide@0.0.0: crt1-reactor.o not found at , the multi-threaded runtime may not be initialized correctly
```

The insiders builds show the same warning, so they are broken too.

This PR:

- Changes `crates/node/build.rs`. For a wasi target, it gets the sysroot with `$RUSTC --print sysroot`, and points `$RUSTC` at the `rustc` of that sysroot before `napi_build::setup()`. It fails the build when `crt1-reactor.o` does not exist. This fixes the wasm build in each environment (release, CI and local), so the workflows need no extra `RUSTC` variable.
- Adds an integration test to `integrations/oxide/wasm.test.ts`. It installs `@tailwindcss/oxide` from the packed tarballs in `dist`, and loads it with `NAPI_RS_FORCE_WASI=error`. It checks that the `.wasm` file exports `_initialize`, and scans a string. It kills `node` after 10s, so a hang fails the test. The test reads no files through WASI, so it runs on Linux and macOS (not on Windows). For this, `exec` in `integrations/utils.ts` gets a `timeout` option, and its error message says `Killed after <timeout>ms` when it kills the command.
- Runs that test file in the `release` and `prepare-release` jobs, before anything is published. On PRs, the `Linux / oxide` integration job runs it.

npm does not allow a second publish of 4.3.4, so the fixed package needs a 4.3.5 release.

## Test plan

- Published tarballs, in a clean npm project with Node 24, with `NAPI_RS_FORCE_WASI=error node -e "require('@tailwindcss/oxide')"`: `4.3.3` returns in 48ms, and `4.3.4` hangs (killed after 20s).
- Before this PR, `RUSTC=rustc pnpm run build:wasm` in `crates/node` prints the `crt1-reactor.o not found at ,` warning. The `.wasm` file has the same exports as `4.3.4` (no `_initialize`), and it hangs in the same way.
- After this PR, the same build prints no warning. The `.wasm` file has the same exports as `4.3.3`, and the package loads in 254ms.
- With a fake `rustc` that gives a sysroot without `crt1-reactor.o`, the build fails with `crt1-reactor.o not found at …`.
- The new integration test passes on macOS with the fixed tarball in `dist`. With the tarball of the build without the fix in `dist`, it fails with `Killed after 10000ms`. With `CI=true`, the release step `pnpm run test:integrations ./integrations/oxide/wasm.test.ts` exits with code 1 after 3 tries (33s).
- `pnpm run build`, the `oxide` integration tests and `pnpm run test` pass.
- The release job cannot run on a PR.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Issues.Title: fix(color-mix): avoid crash when colorspace is missing
Issues.Body:
## Summary
`color-mix(var(--color-red-500))` crashes the build with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'kind')`.

Root cause: the `color-mix()` polyfill in `optimizeAst` unconditionally reads `node.nodes[2]` as the colorspace node. The interpolation method is optional in CSS Color 5, so a single-child `color-mix()` (e.g. one that only contains a `var()`) has no `nodes[2]`, and reading `.kind` crashes.

Fix: guard the access with optional chaining.

## Changes
- `packages/tailwindcss/src/ast.ts`: `colorspace.kind` → `colorspace?.kind`.
- `packages/tailwindcss/src/index.test.ts`: regression test for a `color-mix()` call with no colorspace.

## Testing
```sh
cd packages/tailwindcss
pnpm exec vitest run src/index.test.ts -t "does not crash when the"
pnpm exec vitest run src/index.test.ts -t "color-mix"
```
- Targeted regression test: 1 passed
- All color-mix tests: 15 passed
- Full `src/index.test.ts`: 259 passed (verified by the investigating agent)

## Related
- Fixes #20657

## Checklist
- [x] Regression test added
- [x] No unrelated changes

Issues.Title: `color-mix(var(--color-red-500))` crashes the build with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'kind')`
Issues.Body:
**What version of Tailwind CSS are you using?** v4.3.3. Also `0.0.0-insiders.2626ae6` (current `main`). v4.1.0 has the same problem, v4.0.1 doesn't. **What build tool (or framework if it abstracts the build tool) are you using?** `@tailwindcss/cli` 4.3.3. It also happens on Tailwind Play. **What version of Node.js are you using?** v24.14.1 **What browser are you using?** N/A (the build fails) **What operating system are you using?** Linux **Reproduction URL** https://play.tailwindcss.com/zN8EygDu3C **Describe your issue** A `color-mix(…)` with a single color and no color interpolation method crashes the build when the color is a theme variable: ```html
``` ```css @import "tailwindcss"; ``` ``` $ npx @tailwindcss/cli -i input.css -o out.css Error: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'kind') ``` The CLI exits with code 1 and writes no CSS. In `--watch` mode, the next builds keep failing after the class is removed again, because the compiler keeps the candidate. The same value in plain CSS fails the same way, e.g. `.foo { color: color-mix(var(--color-red-500)); }`. This is valid CSS: in [CSS Color 5](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color-5/#color-mix) the color interpolation method is optional, and `color-mix()` "takes a list of one or more `` specifications": ``` color-mix() = color-mix( ? , [ && ? ]# ) ``` Firefox 158 already accepts `color-mix(red)`. The error comes from the `color-mix(…)` polyfill in `optimizeAst`. To switch the color space of the fallback to `srgb`, it reads the color space from `node.nodes[2]`, which assumes `color-mix(in , …)`. With a single color and no interpolation method, that node doesn't exist: https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/blob/2626ae6c/packages/tailwindcss/src/ast.ts#L585-L587

Issues.Title: Canonicalization: don't sort all parsed variants when compiling a single candidate
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Since #20380, canonicalization compiles every known value of functional variants to look for a canonical name. Each of those compiles calls `getVariantOrder()`, which sorts all parsed variants. Each one also adds a parsed variant, so the cache from #20427 never hits, and the first `canonicalizeCandidates` call gets very slow in projects with many variant values.

In our design system, which has 8 variants with 2,139 values each, the first call went from about 8 seconds in 4.3.3 to about 17 minutes in 4.3.4, so `oxlint-tailwindcss` timed out.

The variant order is only used to sort the rules of different candidates, so this PR skips it when compiling a single candidate. That's what canonicalization does for each variant. Compiling multiple candidates works the same as before, so the generated CSS doesn't change.

Time for the first `canonicalizeCandidates` call with a plugin that registers one `matchVariant` with N values:

| Values | Before | After |
| --: | --: | --: |
| 500 | 281 ms | 16 ms |
| 1,000 | 1,740 ms | 18 ms |

Issues.Title: Negate combined conditions as a whole in `not-*` variants
Issues.Body:
## Summary

`not` in a media, supports or container query only negates the condition right after it. When a variant's condition combines several conditions with `and` or `or`, `not-*` puts `not` in front of the first one only, which gives an invalid query:

```css
@custom-variant tablet (@media (min-width: 768px) and (max-width: 1023px));
```

`not-tablet:flex` generates:

```css
@media not (min-width: 768px) and (max-width: 1023px) {
  .not-tablet\:flex {
    display: flex;
  }
}
```

`not (a) and (b)` doesn't match the grammar, so browsers ignore the rule, and Lightning CSS drops it from an optimized build. The same happens with the built-in `supports-*` variant, e.g. `not-supports-[(display:grid)_and_(gap:1rem)]:flex`, with `or`, and with `@container` queries (named or not). `@media only screen and (…)` has a similar problem: `not only screen and (…)` is invalid too.

This PR wraps a combined condition in parentheses before negating it, and drops `only` from a negated media query:

| Variant condition | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@media (a) and (b)` | `@media not (a) and (b)` | `@media not ((a) and (b))` |
| `@media (a) or (b)` | `@media not (a) or (b)` | `@media not ((a) or (b))` |
| `@media only screen and (a)` | `@media not only screen and (a)` | `@media not screen and (a)` |
| `@supports (a) and (b)` | `@supports not (a) and (b)` | `@supports not ((a) and (b))` |
| `@container (a) and (b)` | `@container not (a) and (b)` | `@container not ((a) and (b))` |
| `@container name (a) and (b)` | `@container name not (a) and (b)` | `@container name not ((a) and (b))` |

A single condition, a media type like `screen and (a)`, and conditions that already start with `not` are negated as before.

## Test plan

- Added a case to the `not` test in `variants.test.ts` with custom variants that use `and`/`or` in `@media` and `@container` (with and without a name), `only screen`, and `not-supports-[(display:grid)_and_(gap:1rem)]`.
- With the fix reverted, the new case fails: every rule is dropped and the output is `""`. With the fix, it passes.
- `vitest run --project tailwindcss`: 45 files, 5189 tests passed, 1 skipped.
- `prettier --check` on the changed files and `pnpm changelog check` pass.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Negate combined conditions as a whole in `not-*` variants" (#20664)

Issues.Title: Keep a declaration without a `;` at the end of the CSS input
Issues.Body:
## Summary

This PR keeps a regular declaration that has no `;` at the end of the CSS input, e.g. `color: red` or `--a: 1;\ncolor: red`. Before, the parser only handled a leftover at-rule after the main loop, so it silently dropped the declaration. PostCSS keeps it (`postcss.parse('color: red')` gives a `decl`), and a top-level declaration that ends with `;` is already kept.

The fix parses the leftover `buffer` as a declaration too, and adds it to the current parent, or to the root. A leftover that is not a declaration (e.g. `foo`) is still ignored, as before, so input that parses today does not start to throw. An unclosed block (e.g. `.foo { color: red`) still throws `Missing closing }`.

A leftover with unbalanced parentheses (e.g. `color: rgb(1, 2`) is not kept, because it is incomplete.

A test also covers a custom property with an unclosed bracket at the end of the input, e.g. `--foo: [bar`. https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20653 makes the rest of the input part of the custom property. Without it, the leftover `-foo: [bar` would become a declaration with this PR.

A user can only reach the bare declaration case through an `@import` inside a rule, e.g. `:root { @import './partial.css'; }`, where the partial ends with a bare declaration. That is not valid CSS, but `substituteAtImports` inlines it, because it walks the whole AST. Thus the value of this fix is small, and the change stays small.

Related: https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20653 (merged) fixed the same problem for custom properties. This PR is rebased on top of it.

## Test plan

- New tests in `packages/tailwindcss/src/css-parser.test.ts` (Unix and Windows line endings) for `color: red`, `color: red\n`, `color: red !important`, `a: 1; b: 2` and `--a: 1;\ncolor: red`. They fail without the fix.
- New tests for `color: rgb(1, 2` (gives `[]`) and for `--foo: [bar` and `color: red; --foo: (bar` (keep the custom property, together with https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20653).
- `pnpm exec vitest run` in `packages/tailwindcss`: all tests pass.
- `pnpm changelog check` passes.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Keep a declaration without a `;` at the end of the CSS input" (#20655)

Issues.Title: Parse a custom property at the end of the input without a trailing `;`
Issues.Body:
## Summary

When a custom property is the last thing in the CSS input and has no `;` or `}` after it, the CSS parser loses part of it:

- `--foo: bar` is parsed as `--foo: ba`. When the scan reaches the last character, it takes `input.slice(start, j)`, which leaves out the character at `j`.
- `--foo: bar !important` is parsed as the non-important `--foo: bar !importan`.
- If the last character is consumed by another branch instead (a closing `)`, a string, a comment or an escape), the loop ends without filling the buffer and the parser emits an empty `: ;` declaration. This happens for `--foo: var(--bar)` or `--foo: 'bar'`, for example.

The existing `should parse a custom property with a missing ending ;` test only passes because its input ends with a newline and indentation.

This can reach the build output through `@import`, when a file of custom properties without a trailing newline is imported inside a rule:

```css
/* input.css */
:root {
  @import './vars.css';
}
```

```css
/* vars.css, no trailing newline */
--brand: red;
--accent: blue
```

This builds to `--accent: blu;`. With `--accent: var(--brand)` it builds to `: ;`.

This PR drops the `input.length - 1 === j` check from the loop. When the loop reaches the end of the input without a `;` or `}` ending the custom property, the rest of the input is used as its value. This matches how PostCSS parses the same input:

| Input | Before | After (same as PostCSS) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--foo: bar` | `--foo: ba` | `--foo: bar` |
| `--foo: bar !important` | `--foo: bar !importan` | `--foo: bar !important` |
| `--foo: var(--x)` | `: ;` | `--foo: var(--x)` |
| `--foo: 'bar'` | `: ;` | `--foo: 'bar'` |
| `--a: 1; --b: 2` | `--a: 1; --b: ;` | `--a: 1; --b: 2` |

## Test plan

- Added a test to `css-parser.test.ts` for a custom property at the end of the input with a plain value, `!important`, `var(…)`, a string, a block, a comment, and after another declaration. Like the other tests in that file, it runs with both Unix and Windows line endings.
- With the fix reverted, the new test fails (`"value": "ba"` instead of `"bar"`). With the fix, it passes.
- `pnpm exec vitest run` in `packages/tailwindcss`: 44 files, 5164 tests passed, 1 skipped.
- `pnpm exec vitest run --project @tailwindcss/node` (it uses this parser to rewrite `url(…)`s in imported files): 8 passed.
- Compared the parsed declarations with `postcss.parse` for the inputs in the table above. They now match.
- `pnpm exec prettier --check` on the changed files passes.

I used Claude Code to write this change.

Issues.Title: Default extractor turns the regex character class in `/[-:T]/g` into a phantom utility `[-:T]`, and the generated declaration `-: T;` breaks Lightning CSS
Issues.Body:
**Title:** Default extractor turns the regex character class in `/[-:T]/g` into a phantom utility `[-:T]`, and the generated declaration `-: T;` breaks Lightning CSS

---

<!-- Please provide all of the information requested below. We're a small team and without all of this information it's not possible for us to help and your bug report will be closed. -->

**What version of Tailwind CSS are you using?**

v3.4.19

**What build tool (or framework if it abstracts the build tool) are you using?**

Vite 8.3.5 (rolldown 1.2.16), `@vitejs/plugin-vue` 6.0.8, postcss 8.5.32, lightningcss 1.33.0 (Vite 8's default CSS minifier), Tailwind used as a PostCSS plugin

**What version of Node.js are you using?**

v24.19.0

**What browser are you using?**

N/A — this is a build-time failure

**What operating system are you using?**

Windows 11

**Reproduction URL**

https://github.com/WangJincheng4869/fanKuiWenJian/tree/main/packages/vite-tailwind

The repo is a fresh `create-vue` (Vite + Vue 3 + TS) project with Tailwind v3 wired in through PostCSS. Only two things matter:

`tailwind.config.js`

```js
export default {
  content: ["./src/**/*.{html,js,vue,ts}"],
};
```

`src/App.vue`

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const downloadPackage = (str: string) => {
  alert(str.slice(0, 19).replace(/[-:T]/g, "").slice(0, 12));
};
</script>

<template>
  <button @click="downloadPackage('2024-55-455T45:55:545')">点击测试</button>
</template>
```

Steps:

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm build-only   # vite build
```

**Describe your issue**

`[-:T]` only exists in this project as the character class inside the regular expression `/[-:T]/g` in a `<script setup>` block. It is never used as a class name anywhere in the template. Still, the default content extractor picks it up as a candidate, treats it as an arbitrary property, and Tailwind generates this rule in the production CSS:

```css
.\[-\:T\] {
  -: T;
}
```

`-` is not a valid CSS property name, so the declaration is invalid, and Lightning CSS (which Vite 8 uses as the default CSS minifier) refuses to parse it. The build stops with:

```
[plugin vite:css-post]
SyntaxError: [lightningcss minify] Unexpected token Semicolon
606 | }
607 | .\[-\:T\] {
608 |   -: T;
    |       ^
609 | }
```

So a plain `.replace()` call that has nothing to do with styling breaks `vite build`, and the error message points at CSS instead of at the source file that contains the regex, which makes it very hard to trace. `vite dev` works because the CSS is not minified there.

The match comes from the "arbitrary properties" pattern in `src/.../tailwindcss/lib/lib/defaultExtractor.js`:

```js
/\[[^\s:'"`]+:[^\s\[\]]+\]/
```

A regex character class of the shape `[a:b]` is textually identical to an arbitrary property `[prop:value]`, so any scanned source containing such a regex (dates, times, sanitizing, slugifying, etc.) produces a phantom utility.

Expected behavior:

- The extractor should not treat a bracketed token that appears in code position — e.g. one immediately preceded by `/`, i.e. inside a regex literal — as a class candidate, so no rule is generated for `[-:T]`.
- Regardless of that, Tailwind should not emit a declaration whose property name is not a valid CSS property name; an unusable candidate like `[-:T]` should be ignored rather than written into the stylesheet.

---

## 中文版

**标题：** 默认提取器把 `/[-:T]/g` 里的正则字符类变成了幻影工具类 `[-:T]`，生成的声明 `-: T;` 让 Lightning CSS 报错

**你使用的 Tailwind CSS 版本是？**

v3.4.19

**你使用的构建工具（或封装了构建工具的框架）是？**

Vite 8.3.5（rolldown 1.2.16）、`@vitejs/plugin-vue` 6.0.8、postcss 8.5.32、lightningcss 1.33.0（Vite 8 默认的 CSS 压缩器），Tailwind 以 PostCSS 插件方式接入

**你使用的 Node.js 版本是？**

v24.19.0

**你使用的浏览器是？**

不涉及 —— 这是构建期失败

**你使用的操作系统是？**

Windows 11

**复现链接**

https://github.com/WangJincheng4869/fanKuiWenJian/tree/main/packages/vite-tailwind

仓库是全新的 `create-vue`（Vite + Vue 3 + TS）项目并接入 Tailwind v3（PostCSS 方式）。只有两处关键内容：

`tailwind.config.js`

```js
export default {
  content: ["./src/**/*.{html,js,vue,ts}"],
};
```

`src/App.vue`

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const downloadPackage = (str: string) => {
  alert(str.slice(0, 19).replace(/[-:T]/g, "").slice(0, 12));
};
</script>

<template>
  <button @click="downloadPackage('2024-55-455T45:55:545')">点击测试</button>
</template>
```

复现步骤：

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm build-only   # 即 vite build
```

**描述你的问题**

`[-:T]` 在项目里只存在于 `<script setup>` 中正则表达式 `/[-:T]/g` 的字符类里，模板中任何位置都没有把它当作 class 使用。但默认的内容提取器仍然把它当成了候选类名，并按 arbitrary property 处理，于是生产构建的 CSS 里出现了这条规则：

```css
.\[-\:T\] {
  -: T;
}
```

`-` 不是合法的 CSS 属性名，这条声明是非法 CSS，而 Lightning CSS（Vite 8 的默认 CSS 压缩器）拒绝解析它，构建直接中断，报错如下：

```
[plugin vite:css-post]
SyntaxError: [lightningcss minify] Unexpected token Semicolon
606 | }
607 | .\[-\:T\] {
608 |   -: T;
    |       ^
609 | }
```

也就是说，一个和样式毫无关系的普通 `.replace()` 调用让 `vite build` 失败了，而且报错指向 CSS，不是指向含这段正则的源文件，极难定位。`vite dev` 正常，因为 dev 下不压缩 CSS。

命中来自 `tailwindcss/lib/lib/defaultExtractor.js` 里那条 "arbitrary properties" 模式：

```js
/\[[^\s:'"`]+:[^\s\[\]]+\]/
```

形如 `[a:b]` 的正则字符类在文本上和 arbitrary property `[prop:value]` 完全一致，所以任何被扫描的源码里只要有这样的正则（日期、时间、清洗、slug 化等场景），都会多出一条幻影工具类。

期望行为：

- 提取器不应把出现在代码位置的方括号内容当作 class 候选，例如紧邻 `/` 之后（即正则字面量内部）的 `[...]`，因此不该为 `[-:T]` 生成任何规则。
- 即便如此，Tailwind 也不该输出属性名并非合法 CSS 属性名的声明；像 `[-:T]` 这种无法使用的候选应当被忽略，而不是写进样式表。

Issues.Title: Keep a single-file `@source` exact when automatic source detection is on
Issues.Body:
With automatic source detection on, `@source "../node_modules/ui-lib/dist/button.js"` scanned every file in `dist/`, so classes from files that were never referenced (e.g. `card.js`) were generated. With `source(none)` the same `@source` was exact. The same thing happens for a file in a gitignored folder.

A file `@source` normally restricts its folder to that file. That step was skipped when the folder sat inside the auto-detected project root, on the assumption that the root already walks it. For ignored folders the root never does, so the folder was walked on its own with no restriction. Now a pattern only counts as covered when the root's walker actually reaches its folder. The check runs a walker with the scanner's own setup from the root toward that folder, so `.gitignore` (including nested whitelists), `.ignore`, `.git/info/exclude` and the default ignored folders all apply exactly as they do for scanning. Explicit folder sources (`@source "../node_modules/ui-lib"`) work as before.

## Test plan

Added scanner tests for a file in `node_modules`, a gitignored folder, a `.ignore`d folder, a `.git/info/exclude`d folder, and a folder re-included by a nested `.gitignore` whitelist. Each fails without the fix and passes with it.

`cargo test -p tailwindcss-oxide`: 125 unit tests and 76 scanner tests pass; `cargo fmt --check` is clean.

Fixes #20637

Issues.Title: Resolve `@import`s that failed in a previous compile once the file exists
Issues.Body:
## Summary

`@tailwindcss/node` creates its CSS and JS resolvers once at module load, each over a `CachedInputFileSystem` with a 4 second cache. In a long-lived process (a dev server, the PostCSS plugin in watch mode) a failed `stat` for an `@import` that doesn't exist yet stays cached, so recompiling right after the file is created still fails with `Can't resolve` until the entry expires.

The three resolvers now share one cached file system, and `compile()` / `compileAst()` purge it before they start. Lookups within a single compile are still cached, but each compile sees the current state of the disk.

Fixes #20638

## Test plan

- Added `packages/@tailwindcss-node/src/compile.test.ts`: compile an `@import` of a missing file (fails), write the file, compile again and expect it to resolve. It fails on `main` with `Can't resolve './accent.css'` and passes with this change.
- `pnpm build && pnpm vitest run`: all unit tests pass.

Issues.Title: @tailwindcss/node: an @import that failed to resolve keeps failing for up to 4 s after the file is written
Issues.Body:
**What version of Tailwind CSS are you using?**

v4.3.3, and `main` at 8cc0551 (`@tailwindcss/node@0.0.0-insiders.8cc0551`)

**What build tool (or framework if it abstracts the build tool) are you using?**

None: `@tailwindcss/node`'s `compile()` called directly from a long-lived process, as a dev server calls it

**What version of Node.js are you using?**

v26.12.1

**What browser are you using?**

N/A

**What operating system are you using?**

Windows

**Reproduction URL**

https://github.com/YevheniiKotyrlo/tailwindcss-import-resolver-cache

**Describe your issue**

In a long-lived process, `compile()` keeps failing an `@import` whose file did not exist at the last compile for up to 4 seconds after the file is written. A dev server that recompiles as soon as its watcher reports the new file gets the same `Can't resolve` again, and stays broken until some later change triggers another compile.

Steps, with the reproduction's `npm install && npm start`:

1. `compile('@import "./accent.css";\n', { base })` in a folder with no `accent.css`: it fails with `Can't resolve './accent.css'`, as expected.
2. Write `accent.css` and call `compile()` again right away.
3. Wait 4.5 s and call `compile()` once more.

Expected: step 2 resolves the import, since the file exists by then.

Seen:

```
before accent.css exists: Can't resolve './accent.css' in 'C:\Users\…\Temp\tailwind-import-ETfnr5'
right after writing accent.css: Can't resolve './accent.css' in 'C:\Users\…\Temp\tailwind-import-ETfnr5'
4.5 s after writing accent.css: resolved
```

The CSS resolver is created once at module load over `new EnhancedResolve.CachedInputFileSystem(fs, 4000)` (`packages/@tailwindcss-node/src/compile.ts`, lines 202-203 at 8cc0551), so the failed `stat` of `accent.css` from step 1 is served from the cache until it expires. The JavaScript resolvers below it use the same cache duration.

**What operating system are you using?**

macOS 26

**Reproduction URL**

https://github.com/pawelkrystkiewicz/tailwind-source-repro

**Describe your issue**

I maintain a React component library, [chunks-ui](https://www.npmjs.com/package/chunks-ui). Since 0.6.0 it ships one CSS file per component, so an app can generate only the classes of the components it renders:

```css
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "chunks-ui/theme.core.css";
@import "chunks-ui/sources/button.css";
```

Each sources file is generated at build time and lists that component's built files with `@source`, for example `@source "../button.js";` and the chunks it imports. Installed from npm, though, an app that imports only `button.css` still gets the classes of every component in the package.

The reproduction strips it down to two files. `ui-lib` is installed from a tarball. `dist/button.js` uses `bg-red-500`, `dist/card.js` uses `bg-blue-500`, and the CSS points at `button.js` only:

```css
@import "tailwindcss";
@source "../node_modules/ui-lib/dist/button.js";
```

| Input | Expected | Actual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@import "tailwindcss"` | `p-4` | `p-4` |
| plus `@source` on `button.js` | `p-4`, `bg-red-500` | `p-4`, `bg-red-500`, `bg-blue-500` |
| `source(none)`, `@source "../src"` and `@source` on `button.js` | `p-4`, `bg-red-500` | `p-4`, `bg-red-500` |

Without automatic detection the `@source` is exact. With it, pointing at one file pulls in every file next to it, so `card.js` is scanned although nothing references it. It looks like the explicit `@source` re-includes the ignored `node_modules/ui-lib/dist` folder and the automatic scan then walks all of it.

Two questions:

1. Is a single-file `@source` meant to stay exact while automatic detection is on? If so, this is a bug, and fixing it would make per-component sources work for libraries as they are.
2. If it is by design: what is the recommended way for a library to let apps generate only the classes of the components they import, now that the Vite plugin no longer reads the module graph (#16631)? `source(none)` works, but then every app has to list its own folders with `@source`, and a folder it forgets renders unstyled.

Related: #19684 and #19959 ask for the same outcome from the library side.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "`@source` on one file inside `node_modules` scans the file's whole folder when automatic detection is on" (#20637)

Issues.Title: Fix stale file reads during a CLI rebuild
Issues.Body:
## Summary

A rename that lands while a CLI rebuild is running keeps the first read of that file. Later renames were dropped until the follow-up rebuild started, so that rebuild compiled the first snapshot.

The raw handler marks the file pending, reads it, then awaits `recordChangedFile`. While the rebuild was still running, a later rename saw the pending slot and returned. The slot was cleared when the follow-up rebuild started.

Store one pending change per file and run one rebuild at a time. `recordChangedFile` resolves immediately, so a later rename replaces the queued read. The value passed to `rebuild()` is unchanged: `{ file, content, extension }`.

## Test plan

- `npx jest tests/watching.test.js --runInBand` — 2 passed, on Node 22.
- The same file against the unpatched watcher fails the rename test. The follow-up keeps `page 0` and `view 0` instead of `page 7` and `view 7`.
- `npx eslint src/cli/build/watching.js tests/watching.test.js` — clean.

Repeated `change` events were already collapsed by `pendingRebuilds`. The new assertion is the rename case.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Fix stale file reads during a CLI rebuild" (#20636)

Issues.Title: Extract classes from multi-line Ruby in Haml templates
Issues.Body:
## Summary

In Haml, a line of Ruby can continue onto the next lines as long as each line but the last ends with a comma:

```haml
= render("card",
  title: "Hello",
  class: "bg-[#f8f5ff] min-w-[140px]")
```

`skip_indented_block` only keeps the first line of that Ruby code. On the next line it stops at the first non-whitespace character (`_ => break`), so the continuation lines are processed as Haml instead of Ruby: the top-level `[`, `]` and `#` get replaced with spaces and candidates like `bg-[#f8f5ff]` and `min-w-[140px]` are never extracted. The same file renamed to `.erb` or `.rb` extracts them fine.

This keeps consuming a line when the previous line ended with a comma, for `=` and `-` lines, so the whole expression goes through the Ruby pre-processor. Haml comments (`-#` and `/`) are left alone, so a comment ending in a comma doesn't swallow the line after it.

We found this in a Rails app, where classes passed to multi-line `render` and `link_to` calls were missing from the build.

One fixture changes: in `dst-17051.haml` a `href: "https://…/loco_motion#locomotion-components"` continuation line no longer yields `locomotion-components` (the fragment of the URL), because it's now handled as a Ruby string, like it would be in a `.rb` file.

## Test plan

Added `test_multi_line_ruby` to `haml.rs`, covering `=` and `-` continuations, a nested block, and a comment ending in a comma. Without the change it fails with `bg-[#f8f5ff]`, `min-w-[140px]`, `text-[#0b3fa8]` and `w-[240px]` missing.

```sh
cargo test -p tailwindcss-oxide
rustfmt --check --edition 2021 crates/oxide/src/extractor/pre_processors/haml.rs
```
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Extract classes from multi-line Ruby in Haml templates" (#20635)

Issues.Title: Performance: reuse dynamic utility lookups across canonicalizeCandidates collapse groups
Issues.Body:
### Summary

In Tailwind CSS **4.3.3**, `canonicalizeCandidates(..., { collapse: true, logicalToPhysical: true })` repeatedly builds the same dynamic-utility alternatives when called for many class groups in a lint run.

A small experimental cache scoped to the **design-system object + SignatureOptions object + candidate string** reduced a canonical-rule-only lint workload from **12.3s to 10.7s**, and **12.1s to 10.5s**, in sequential A/B/A/B runs. This is a modest application-specific improvement, not a claim of a general 2x speedup or an end-to-end build improvement.

### Source hotspot

Tagged source: https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/blob/v4.3.3/packages/tailwindcss/src/canonicalize-candidates.ts#L339-L375

Inside `collapseCandidates` → `collapseGroup`, a fresh `dynamicUtilities = new DefaultMap(...)` is created for every group. Its factory:

1. Looks up the candidate's relevant properties.
2. Iterates the functional utility roots.
3. Compiles/looks up replacements with the same value/modifier and builds property/value → replacement sets.

The underlying utility-property lookups are cached, but rebuilding and iterating this alternatives map is repeated. The factory appears to depend on the design system, signature options, and candidate—not the other candidates in the current group.

### Measurement setup

- Tailwind CSS 4.3.3; eslint-plugin-better-tailwindcss 4.9.1; Oxlint 1.87.0.
- Linux containers under Dagger, Node 26.12.1-slim.
- 769 web files. Native syntax lint remained enabled; only the Tailwind canonical-class rule was enabled among the Tailwind rules. Type-aware lint was disabled for this experiment.
- Default canonical rule options: collapse=true, logicalToPhysical=true, rem unspecified.
- Fresh Node/linter processes, same application source and configuration, sequential baseline/candidate/baseline/candidate in one container invocation.
- Both variants used the same instrumentation, including cumulative high-resolution timers and thread CPU counters. Absolute timings include instrumentation overhead and are not a rigorous general-purpose benchmark.
- The application corpus is not a standalone public reproducer; the source hotspot and regression examples below are the actionable parts of this report.

| Measurement | Baseline 1 | Candidate 1 | Baseline 2 | Candidate 2 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Oxlint-reported whole lint wall time | 12.3s | 10.7s | 12.1s | 10.5s |
| Canonical worker total, wall | 9.449s | 7.939s | 9.252s | 7.825s |
| canonicalizeCandidates calls, wall | 9.011s | 7.511s | 8.842s | 7.429s |
| canonicalizeCandidates calls, thread user+system CPU | 6.628s | 6.052s | 6.605s | 5.900s |
| Dynamic-alternatives factory evaluations | 5,937 | 905 | 5,938 | 905 |
| Dynamic factory, wall | 3.759s | 2.236s | 3.545s | 2.285s |
| Dynamic factory, thread user+system CPU | 2.137s | 1.622s | 1.983s | 1.615s |

All four full-corpus runs produced zero warnings/errors. Worker group counts varied slightly (~1,423–1,443) because the caller has a shared LRU and parallel file scheduling changes eviction order.

Additional attribution from an instrumented baseline:

- CSS/design-system loading was ~79ms, once—not the multi-second bottleneck.
- The first lazy canonicalization call took ~3.0s. That initialization cost remains with the candidate.
- Per-candidate canonicalization/cache lookup total was ~4.17s wall; full group collapsing accounted for another ~4.48s.
- The caller made 2,468 operation-cache lookups, with ~1,024–1,039 hits and only 14–29 eviction misses in representative runs. This was not mainly a too-small caller cache.
- Prefix IPC was measured separately (~0.4s wall in that baseline). The candidate does not optimize prefix handling.

### Minimal optimization sketch

Add one storage slot to the canonicalization DesignSystem interface:

~~~ts
[DYNAMIC_UTILITIES_KEY]: WeakMap<
  SignatureOptions,
  DefaultMap<string, DefaultMap<string, DefaultMap<string, Set<string>>>>
>
~~~

Then reuse the existing factory instead of changing its algorithm:

~~~ts
const DYNAMIC_UTILITIES_KEY = Symbol()

// Inside collapseGroup, after obtaining signatureOptions and the existing lookups:
const cache = (designSystem.storage[DYNAMIC_UTILITIES_KEY] ??= new WeakMap())
let dynamicUtilities = cache.get(signatureOptions)
if (!dynamicUtilities) {
  dynamicUtilities = new DefaultMap(/* existing candidate factory, unchanged */)
  cache.set(signatureOptions, dynamicUtilities)
}

// Keep the existing property intersections, linked candidates, combinations,
// signature equivalence tests, and complete group collapse algorithm unchanged.
~~~

The benchmark candidate made the equivalent narrow change to the installed ESM distribution in a temporary container. No application patch or rule removal is proposed.

### Semantics and cache lifetime

This is **not** a per-class canonicalization shortcut. Two individually canonical classes can still collapse together (e.g. px-2 + py-2 → p-2), and every complete group still goes through the existing collapse algorithm.

- Cache separation follows the same SignatureOptions identity as the existing property/signature caches, preserving distinctions such as rem, property expansion, and logical-to-physical handling.
- Cache storage belongs to the actual design-system object. Replacing/reloading that object yields an empty cache, just like the existing internal canonicalization caches.
- This does not introduce a new process-global stylesheet cache, and does not claim to fix the caller's existing stylesheet dependency invalidation. Persistent-editor/CSS reload behavior should receive upstream tests before adopting it.
- The new map retains alternatives until the design system is discarded; memory impact has not been quantified.

### Diagnostic equivalence checked

I compared the actual linter's complete JSON diagnostics before/after the candidate for fixtures containing:

~~~tsx
<div className="w-[1rem]" />
<div className="px-2 py-2" />
<div className="sm:px-2 sm:py-2" />
<div className="px-2! py-2!" />
<div className="flex-grow" />
<div className="ps-2 pe-2" />
<div className={"px-2 py-2 " + suffix} />
~~~

Both variants emitted **the same 10 diagnostics**, including single-candidate w-[1rem] → w-4 and flex-grow → grow, two-input collapse, variant/important handling, and concatenated-literal handling. The entire test was repeated with a real `prefix(tw)` stylesheet and tw:-prefixed classes: again **10 identical diagnostics**. JSON equality included messages, severities, file names and source spans. Autofix output and the full Tailwind upstream test suite were not tested.

Would a design-system-scoped cache for this particular lookup be appropriate upstream? The observed gain is useful but limited (~1.6s/~13% in this lint workload); the remaining lazy initialization and other canonicalization costs are deliberately not presented as solved.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "Performance: reuse dynamic utility lookups across canonicalizeCandidates collapse groups" (#20634)
